The phone is not on a network. Turn on Wi-Fi or mobile data.
Wi-Fi is connected, but there is no internet behind it. Hotels and cafés do this — there is a sign-in page to open.
Aeroplane mode is on.
Android is asking permission, and without it I cannot open the path. It is the ordinary system dialog.
Another VPN app is running. Only one can be at a time.
The phone put me to sleep, so the connection dropped. This is fixed once and stays fixed.
The phone is cutting my work off in the background to save battery.
I could not read this key. It looks as though it was not copied whole.
The key has no outpost address in it. Ask for it to be sent again.
The key points at a page that is not answering. This is usually temporary.
This key works by a method I cannot do yet.
There is no key yet. Paste one — it is the only thing needed.
I cannot find the outpost by its name. Your provider may be spoiling the address book.
The outpost says this door is shut. Something has most likely changed on the server.
The outpost is not answering. Either it is switched off, or we are not being let through to it.
The outpost refused the handshake. This usually means the server was updated and the key was not.
The outpost did not recognise me. The key has most likely been revoked or has expired.
Something has stepped between me and the outpost and is pretending to be it. It is not safe to connect.
Your network is not letting this kind of connection through today. I have tried every way round I know.
Your provider is throttling the connection after the first few kilobytes. Moving to a method that gets round it.
The path is open but narrow — your provider is slowing it. I will look for a wider one.
This method does not get through on your mobile operator, though it is fine over Wi-Fi.
Something broke inside me. That is my fault, not yours.
This build does not suit your phone. A different version of the app is needed.
I cannot open the key store. This happens after the screen lock is changed.
